purpose: liblhasa is a library for reading and decompressing LHA archives.

functions.lha_reader_current_is_fake: Returns whether the current entry is a synthetic one: a fake directory or a deferred symlink. Call it on a valid `LHAReader*` after selecting/reading the current entry; it returns nonzero for those two cases, 0 otherwise.
functions.lha_reader_check: `lha_reader_check` verifies the current entry: it returns 1 for directories, 0 if the current file isn’t a normal file, and otherwise opens the decoder and fully decodes the file to validate it (e.g., CRC). Use it only on the current normal file entry; it may invoke the progress callback during decoding.
functions.lha_decoder_monitor: Sets a progress callback for `LHADecoder`. Use it before/while decoding to receive progress updates via `callback_data`. It scales `block_size` up for very large streams so reported blocks stay ≤128K and avoid 32-bit overflow, then triggers an initial progress check.
functions.lha_reader_read: `lha_reader_read` reads decompressed bytes from the current file. Call it after selecting/opening an entry; on first use it lazily creates the decoder. It returns bytes read, or `0` if decoder setup fails or no more data is available.
functions.lha_reader_extract: `lha_reader_extract` extracts the current entry from an `LHAReader`. Use it after positioning on a file; `filename` can override the output path, and `callback` reports progress for normal files. Returns 1 on success, 0 if at START/EOF or unsupported state.
functions.lha_decoder_free: `lha_decoder_free` destroys an `LHADecoder`. It first calls the decoder type’s optional `free` hook on the decoder-specific data (`decoder+1`), then frees the decoder object itself. Use it once when done; if no type-specific cleanup exists, only the object is freed.
functions.lha_reader_free: `lha_reader_free` destroys an `LHAReader`. Use it when you're done with the reader. It closes any active decoder, frees all stacked directory/file headers, frees the internal basic reader, then frees the reader object itself.
functions.lha_reader_next_file: Advances `reader` to the next `LHAFileHeader`, closing any current decoder first. It returns `NULL` at EOF. If the previous item was a fake dir, it frees it; on normal/start entries it advances the underlying reader before handling queued directory entries.
functions.lha_input_stream_from: Creates an `LHAInputStream` from a file path. It opens `filename` in binary mode, wraps the `FILE*`, and returns `NULL` if `fopen` fails or stream creation fails. On creation failure, it closes the file.
functions.lha_decoder_for_name: Looks up a decoder type by its string name. Pass a NUL-terminated `name`; it scans the built-in decoder table and returns the matching `LHADecoderType *`. If no match is found, it returns `NULL` (also unsafe if `name` is `NULL`).
functions.lha_input_stream_free:
`lha_input_stream_free` destroys an `LHAInputStream`: if the stream type has a `close` callback, it closes the underlying handle, then frees the stream object itself. Use it when you’re done with the input stream; it’s safe even if no close handler exists.
Only pass a valid, fully initialized LHAInputStream created by supported constructors such as lha_input_stream_from() or lha_input_stream_from_FILE(). Do not call lha_input_stream_free() on an object returned from lha_input_stream_new(NULL, NULL) or any stream whose type field may be NULL. Before freeing, ensure the stream pointer is non-NULL and was successfully constructed with a non-NULL LHAInputStreamType.
functions.lha_reader_new: Creates a new `LHAReader` around an `LHAInputStream`. Use it to start reading an LHA archive. Returns `NULL` on allocation failure or if `lha_basic_reader_new(stream)` fails; otherwise initializes state to start-of-archive defaults.
functions.lha_decoder_read: `lha_decoder_read` copies up to `buf_len` decompressed bytes into `buf` and returns the number copied. It truncates at `stream_length` to avoid extra false bytes. Use it repeatedly until it returns 0/end-of-stream; it may return less than requested if data remains buffered or at EOF.
functions.lha_decoder_get_length64: Returns the decoder’s current output length/position (`stream_pos`) as a 64-bit value. Call it on a valid `LHADecoder` after/while decoding to query how many bytes have been processed. It just returns the stored counter; no extra validation or side effects.
functions.lha_reader_set_dir_policy: Sets how `LHAReader` handles directory entries during extraction/listing. Call it on an initialized `LHAReader` before reading entries. It just stores `policy` in `reader->dir_policy`; no validation or side effects.
functions.lha_decoder_get_crc: Returns the decoder’s current CRC value. Use it after/while decoding to inspect the running checksum state. It just reads `decoder->crc` and does no validation, update, or error handling.
functions.lha_input_stream_new:
Creates an `LHAInputStream` wrapper around a user-provided `handle` and stream `type`. Use it to initialize a new input stream object; it allocates and zeroes the struct, sets `INIT` state, or returns `NULL` on allocation failure.
This constructor allocates a new LHAInputStream with calloc(), so every successful call must have a matching lha_input_stream_free(). Ensure cleanup is performed on all paths, including normal completion and error handling. Avoid double-management by defining clear ownership: either the caller frees the returned stream, or ownership is explicitly transferred to another API that documents it will free the stream.
functions.lha_decoder_new64: Creates a new decoder and allocates one block for the object, algorithm private data, and output buffer. Use with a valid `dtype`, callback, user data, and `stream_length`. On allocation failure it returns `NULL`; otherwise fields are initialized, including `stream_pos=0` and `crc=0`.
functions.lha_input_stream_from_FILE:
Wraps an existing `FILE*` as an `LHAInputStream` without taking ownership. It first sets the stream to binary mode, then creates the input stream using the unowned file source. Use it for already-open `FILE*`; the caller still closes the `FILE*`.
This API returns a heap-allocated LHAInputStream wrapper for the provided FILE*. Treat the returned pointer as an owned object that must be released with lha_input_stream_free() when no longer needed. Do not assume fclose(FILE*) frees the wrapper. If the stream is passed to another object such as LHAReader, verify ownership semantics from the API contract; if ownership is not explicitly transferred, keep responsibility for calling lha_input_stream_free(stream) on the success path.
